_comment: PHV5-041 acceptance corpus for the PreToolUse:Bash guard. This is the FALSIFIER:
a matcher that fails any row here fails the ticket, whatever its implementation.
This corpus lives in a FILE, not in test command lines, for a reason discovered
while writing it: the live guard denies any Bash command whose text contains a
trigger string, so a harness that passes payloads as shell arguments gets blocked
before it can run. That is F24 reproducing itself against its own test suite.
want_exit: 0 = allow (or ask, which is also exit 0 with JSON), 2 = deny.
want_decision: expected permissionDecision once F22/F26 land; null = no JSON needed.

cases.why: F25: --force-with-lease is the safe form and must be allowed. A '--force\b' pattern matches INSIDE it because '-' is a word boundary.

The reproduction payload named verbatim in the F24 acceptance row. A real force-push in a compound command must be denied via the PARSED tool_input.command — the quoted commit message must not shield it.
F25: the unqualified long flag must be denied.
F25: bare -f is the same operation and must be denied.
F24 core: the danger string appears only inside a quoted argument. Tokenize or strip quoted spans before matching; a bare regex over the raw command denies this.

tool_input.command: git commit -m "never use git push --force on main"

cases.why: F24 cross-field decoy: enforce only what is parsed from tool_input.command. NOTE this row is necessary but NOT sufficient — mutation M4 proved it cannot detect a raw-payload grep for '"command":', because 'description' is a different key name and the grep still finds the right field. F24-decoy-sibling-key-allow is the row that discriminates.

F24 field-blindness, the discriminating form: a SIBLING object carries its own 'command' key holding a danger string, serialized BEFORE tool_input. A first-match grep for '"command":"[^"]*"' picks up meta.command and denies a benign 'ls'. Only extraction of the named tool_input.command path allows this. Added after mutation M4 escaped the weaker decoy row.
F24 cross-field decoy in a different field name.

tool_input.content: reminder: supabase db push is banned

cases.why: Audit v1 gap 2, reproduced live: the current guard denies a read-only grep whose SEARCH PATTERN contains a DB-deploy string.
F22: destructive-but-legitimate. Must be permissionDecision 'ask' at exit 0, never a deny, and never stderr on exit 0 (F26).
Ledger row 1: the DB-deploy guard exists ONLY inline today. It must survive the port, and must run BEFORE the non-git early-exit.
Ledger row 1 exemption: --dry-run validates without deploying.
Ledger row 1 ordering proof: this command is NOT a git command, so any DB guard placed below the 'git (commit|push) || exit 0' line is dead code and this row passes only if the guard runs first.

Exemption tokens count only inside the command field. The token is embedded in a space-delimited sentence so that a whitespace-anchored regex applied to the RAW payload WOULD match it — the earlier form ('--dry-run' alone) was quote-wrapped in the JSON and matched neither way, so mutation M8 escaped it. Now the row discriminates.
3.1.6: a malformed payload under a REAL parser fails closed. Distinct from having no parser at all, which allows.
Nothing to enforce means nothing to deny — never deny on an absent field.
The '"command":"[^"]*"' grep truncates at the first quote, so an escaped quote inside the command silently changes what gets matched.
